correctness.rationale: For every m>=2, P3/P4 and P2 give meet-dependence and consequent monotonicity; P1/P2 and conditional identity force 1→b=b and 0→b=1. Holliday Prop.1 antitone negation, semicomplementation and a<=¬¬a force exactly j=0,...,m, with ¬u=c_j (j>0) and ¬c_i=u iff i<=j. For i<=j, P2 plus the u lower bound forces all positive lower chain consequences to 1. For i>j, the row is an extensive monotone idempotent ceiling map on its chain interval, fixing 0 and top, and P5 enforces nested lower fixed-point sets F_i. Conversely, for any nested such sets, P5 is checked on d=a∧b=0,u,c_k(k<=j),c_k(k>j), with all other axioms immediate. Each c_s has independent first-activation index in max(s+1,j+1)..m or never, yielding m! for j=0 and (m-j+1)^j(m-j)! for j>0, with injectivity and no nontrivial L_m automorphisms. Independent from the bundled code, complete row-candidate enumeration (all meet-dependent monotone extensive semicomplementary rows then the literal P5/DNI) counted m=1..4: 2,5,17,75 and a pairwise-P5 backtracking enumeration counted ALL m=5 tables: 407 with j-fibers 120,120,96,54,16,1. The universal theorem rests on the proof, not these finite runs.
residual_risks: No mechanical proof of all m; the written structural P5 case split supplies the universal argument.
Independent m=6 brute-force attempt exceeded its bounded runtime and is not evidence against the theorem or needed to validate the all-m proof.

value.rationale: L_2=N5 is the standard minimal nonmodular pentagon and lengthening its chain arm yields a natural infinite family of nondistributive bounded lattices. The theorem is a complete structural classification of F-preconditional expansions on this family, identifying the interaction of forced negation thresholds and independent consequent fixed-point activations; it is not a tiny parameter slice or mere recurrence fitting. The exact cardinality coincides with the already-known OEIS A129591 permutation sequence, so the numerical sequence alone has no new value; the motivated contribution is a new algebraic interpretation plus normal form on natural nonchain objects, extending the previously known finite-chain case.
residual_risks: Usefulness is limited to this precise F hierarchy and two-arm family; no general all-lattice enumeration or broader logical consequence is claimed.
If an older directly applicable general theorem is located, value/originality should be reassessed in light of its implication.

final_claim: For every integer m>=2, on L_m with 0<c1<...<cm<1 and 0<u<1 incomparable with all ci, the F-preconditionals satisfying P1–P5, conditional identity, semicomplementation and double-negation inflation are in bijection with a threshold j in {0,...,m} and independent fixed-point activation times tau_s in {max(j+1,s+1),...,m,m+1} for 1<=s<m; their number is A_m=m!+sum_{j=1}^m (m-j+1)^j(m-j)!, with no nontrivial lattice automorphisms for m>=2.
limitations: The exact numerical sequence is pre-existing OEIS A129591, though the lattice normal form is not directly implied by its permutation interpretation.
Complete finite exhaustive all-row checks end at m=5; all m>=2 depends on a direct formal mathematical classification argument.
The arbitrary K-preconditional class, all nonmodular lattices, categorical relational representations and enumeration of all representation frames are out of scope.
